chunks: From him, from al-Husayn, from Aban, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do I pray the obligatory prayer with Umm Ali?' He said, 'Yes, it will be to your right; its prostration will be in line with your feet.'

key_terms.أُمِّ عَلِيٍّ: Umm Ali (a specific prayer mat or rug)
key_terms.سُجُودُهَا: Its prostration (referring to the place of prostration on the mat)

ai.seo_question: Where should the prayer mat be placed relative to the worshipper during obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the proper placement of the *sajjada* (prayer mat) and the alignment of the forehead during prostration, emphasizing precision in ritual posture. The instruction to place the mat on the right and align the prostration with the feet reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and physical correctness in *salah*, ensuring the worshipper’s focus remains undisturbed by misalignment. This detail underscores the broader principle that even minor aspects of prayer geometry contribute to the spiritual integrity of the act of worship.
